text:
kevin: thinking out loud — want to explore adding a lightweight request "snapshotting" layer to the gateway so streaming clients can soft-reconnect after transient network blips without restarting from zero. tradeoffs?

maria: interesting. is the idea that the gateway would emit a resume token and keep a compact snapshot of in-flight state?

kevin: yeah, small resume token + server-side checkpoint. token contains version, offset, and an hmac. server keeps a bounded snapshot (KV of last N tokens / offsets). client reconnects with token to resume streaming.

anya: what counts as "state" here? model kv cache pointers, recent prefixes, and finalizer flags? storing full KV cache per request isn't possible. we'd need to only persist metadata (sequence idx, model variant, user-visible prefix length).

kevin: exactly. snapshot = {model_id, model_version, prefix_len, last_emitted_token_id, admission_stamp}. not the full KV cache. when resuming, runtime attempts to replay from prefix + model fast-path; if mismatch we fallback to a restart.

dave: big concern: side effects. many endpoints call downstream services during generation (billing, webhooks). resuming could cause duplicate side effects. we need a rule: allow resume only for idempotent or read-only flows, or require client-provided idempotency-key for side-effecting ops.

maria: agree. enforce resume for endpoints that declare "resumable:true" in route config. for others we reject resume attempts with 409. docs + openapi-ish flag.

anya: also consider billing semantics. if client reconnects and we replay tokens we must avoid double-billing. maybe bill on finalization (when stream completes) rather than chunk emission? that changes telemetry.

kevin: alternative: charge in two phases — provisional tokens charged when emitted, but if resume occurs we reconcile. ugly. preferable: keep accounting idempotent by attaching stream-instance-id to billing events and dedupe server-side.

dave: how long do we retain snapshots? TTL tradeoffs: shorter TTL => less mem, worse UX. suggest default 30s, configurable per-customer route. snapshots are stored in-memory LRU per edge node; longer-lived customers can opt into Dedicated-managed state store.

maria: security: resume token must be unforgeable and short-lived. HMAC with route-specific key + expiry, or use signed JWT-like token with kid pointing at KMS key. do not encode secrets/state in plaintext.

kevin: proposed header: `X-Redwood-Resume: <base64(hdr)>`. hdr fields: version|exp|node_id|stream_id|hmac. on resume gateway validates hmac & expiry, looks up snapshot. if snapshot missing -> 410 (gone) fallback hint to restart.

anya: operationally we need metrics: resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, resume_fallbacks->restart, resume_memory_bytes, per-route latency delta when resuming.

maria: runtime risks: if we accept resume we must ensure KV cache/quantization branch matches or provide a safe fast-path. otherwise resumed responses could degrade quality. need runtime invariant checks.

kevin: implementation sketch: 1) gateway emits resume token after initial handshake + first chunk; 2) snapshot kept in gateway edge memory keyed by stream_id; 3) on reconnect client sends token; gateway validates and either fast-resume (reseed runtime with prefix_len) or responds with 410; 4) fall back to normal restart with logging.

dave: fallback routing: if edge node lost snapshot, we could try lookup in central snapshot-store (optional). that supports multi-node handoffs but increases complexity + consistency. better to start single-node only.

maria: test plan: property tests for idempotency/dedupe billing, chaos tests where snapshots evict mid-stream, perf microbench for memory/allocs, and an e2e with a flaky mobile client. add route-level opt-in flag.

anya: security checklist: token rotation cadence, KMS integration, audit logs that show resume requests and outcome, scrub sensitive prompt content from snapshot. snapshots must not contain user prompt text (only prefix length and model pointers).

kevin: one more thought: for private deployments we can expose a deployment option to persist snapshots to customer-managed Redis to support longer windows without centralizing data. must document privacy implications.

deploy-bot: feature-flag created: `edge.resume-snapshotting` (disabled by default). CI job `resume-integration` added to nightly.

maria: proposed action items: 1) write short RFC that includes: API header, token format, retention defaults, resume route opt-in, billing dedupe model, and failure codes (410/409/422), 2) prototype single-node gateway snapshotter, 3) perf & churn tests.

kevin: +1 to RFC. I'll draft initial doc and drop in #architecture next week. tagging @anya and @dave for implementation follow-up. :thumbsup:

anya: will sketch runtime checks for fast-path safety and send a PR for invariants.

dave: I'll own billing dedupe and route-config integration.

maria: thanks — this addresses a lot of customer pain with flaky mobile connections. keep the resume window conservative at first. :+1:
